title: Manage Sub-Scope Documents
summary: let the existing source and metadata editors act on an explicitly supplied parent or sub-scope document identity without changing report selection
content_html:
Manage Sub-Scope Documents

Result

Local Docs Viewer management can open the existing Markdown source editor and Edit metadata modal for a displayed document in a configured one-level sub-scope without adding that document to the parent scope's index panel.

The public report UI and minimal payload schema remain unchanged; edited content, metadata, and visibility flow through their normal projections. The management capability is reusable for sub-scopes rather than being part of the Tag Registry workflow.

Why this is separate

Embedded Detail Documents deliberately leaves the indexed parent report selected while its report owns the active subdoc. Source and metadata editing must therefore receive an explicit target rather than treating the displayed or selected document as an implicit write target. That identity bridge is a Docs Viewer management capability, not a tag-document association concern.

Tag-document linking can author either viewable state and its current migration contract chooses public documents. The migration nevertheless depends on this feature: direct source editing in an external editor is not a sufficient management workflow for the large document set it will create.

Current starting point

  • The public docs_subscope report already lists configured sub-scope documents and renders a listed subdoc without putting it in the sidebar.
  • A sub-scope manifest is a flat public list and existence payload, not an index tree. A sub-scope may contain hundreds of documents, so the payload stays tight: it exposes only fields required by public report listing, validation, navigation, and deliberately supported filtering. Its flat structure and its cardinality are independent.
  • The local Markdown Source editor currently derives its target from the selected parent document.
  • Edit metadata currently hydrates and saves an indexed parent-scope document and always includes the Parent field.
  • Docs Viewer reports are read-oriented surfaces. They may drive navigation, but they should not become owners of source-write workflows.

Selected UI contract

The existing docs_subscope report remains the navigation and rendered-detail host. It does not become a source editor.

The management toolbar projects the rendered document and source-mode actions explicitly:

state Edit metadata report source subdoc source Return to doc
rendered report list parent report enabled for the parent report disabled unavailable
rendered valid subdoc detail displayed subdoc enabled for the parent report enabled for the displayed subdoc unavailable
Markdown source unavailable disabled disabled enabled

The existing report Source action always supplies the parent report's { scope, doc_id }, including while a subdoc detail is displayed. The new subdoc Source action is enabled only after the report has validated and displayed a listed detail; it supplies { scope, sub_scope, doc_id }.

The existing Edit metadata action follows the rendered target. On the report list it receives the explicit parent { scope, doc_id }; on a validated subdoc detail it receives the explicit { scope, sub_scope, doc_id }. The sub-scope modal keeps every existing metadata control except Parent: Title, Summary, Date, Date display, Status, and non-viewable remain editable. It neither sends nor mutates parent_id.

The report has separate public and management data inputs. Public mode receives only the tight public manifest and renders no Status or non-viewable icons. Manage mode receives one compact local inventory of every sub-scope document, keyed by doc_id, with title, ui_status, and viewable; it uses the existing icons for those two states. It does not fetch hundreds of by-ID payloads to construct the list.

Source entry is no longer a toggle. In source mode both entry actions remain visible but disabled, and the explicit Return to doc action restores the unchanged rendered route. The parent report remains selected and the subdoc query parameter is preserved.

The existing source editor remains the only editor surface. Its body-only buffer, dirty-state prompt, stale-revision protection, Save/Rebuild, Add image, Add file, Add catalogue token, contextual token Info view, and other registered source-editor contributions remain valid. Save/Rebuild keeps its current successful return to rendered view; Return to doc owns the explicit leave-without-rebuild path and its existing dirty-state prompt.

Required identity and write boundary

  • The source editor and metadata workflow require a supplied target. Neither defaults to the displayed document, selected index document, URL doc, or URL subdoc.
  • A parent target is { scope, doc_id }.
  • A sub-scope target is { scope, sub_scope, doc_id }.
  • The parent report remains selected in the index panel, and no sub-scope records are merged into the parent index-tree.json.
  • Every source-file action uses the active supplied target. Read, rebuild, and Open in VS Code carry sub_scope for a sub-scope target; buffer-only contributions act on the same active editor adapter.
  • The service resolves only configured one-level sub-scope roots, validates the document identity, preserves the existing source revision contract, and performs the targeted sub-scope document and search rebuild.
  • Edit metadata hydrates the full source record through the local management service using the supplied target. It does not add management fields to the tight public manifest or compact public by-ID payload.
  • The local management inventory includes all sub-scope documents, including non-viewable documents. The public manifest contains only publicly eligible basic identities and remains { doc_id, title }.
  • Sub-scope metadata writes preserve the existing Title, Summary, Date, Date display, Status, and viewable contracts. They reject parent_id, preserve any source value unchanged, and retain the existing public projection behavior for viewable.
  • A successful sub-scope rebuild refreshes the embedded detail payload without selecting the subdoc in the parent index or treating it as a parent-scope document.
  • Missing or unlisted targets show a contained unavailable state and cannot resolve an arbitrary source path.

Boundary

In scope:

  • the current report list and rendered detail navigation;
  • explicit parent and subdoc source-entry controls;
  • explicit source and metadata target handoff;
  • the existing body-only Markdown Source mode;
  • dirty-state, stale-revision, save, rebuild, source contributions, and return behavior;
  • the existing Edit metadata modal for configured sub-scope documents, with only Parent omitted;
  • Title, Summary, Date, Date display, Status, and viewable editing;
  • the compact manage-only inventory and existing Status/non-viewable icons in the manage report;
  • focused source read, metadata read/write, rebuild, open, and rendered-detail refresh support for configured one-level sub-scopes; and
  • unchanged public report UI and minimal manifest schema.

Not in scope:

  • a separate local manage report;
  • creating, deleting, moving, or transferring sub-scope documents;
  • adding sub-scope documents to the parent index, Recent, or global search;
  • public source editing; or
  • turning reports into general write-capable workflow hosts; or
  • a second or reduced-capability source editor.

Feature document

  • Sub-Scope Document Editing Delivery — proposed explicit-target source, metadata, service, and reload integration.

Downstream consequence

The future Tag semantic-token target waits indirectly on this feature because the tag-document migration is blocked here. Semantic-token registration is not part of this feature; it follows only after tag targets have stable document associations and workable public detail URLs.

Possible future enhancement

A separate low-priority enhancement may add optional ui_status to the public by-ID payload of a publicly eligible sub-scope document and render the existing status badge in that document's detail header. It would not add ui_status or viewable to the public manifest, add icons to public report rows, or make the parent document's info panel subdoc-aware. This delivery keeps ui_status management-only.

Durable destinations

If shipped, the stable embedded-detail identity and navigation behavior belongs in Embedded Detail Documents. The stable report-host boundary belongs in Reports. Source-editor behavior belongs with the existing Docs Viewer management and source-editing documentation. Metadata mutation and viewable behavior belong with their existing maintained contracts.
